evidenceTier.A: Peer-reviewed and replicated/consistent body of evidence. In this first canonicalization, A is retained only where the source package explicitly assigned A.
evidenceTier.B: Peer-reviewed single strong study or robust historical literature; also the conservative default for established legacy items without an explicit A/B tier.
evidenceTier.C: Credible working paper/preprint, promising single finding, model benchmark, or research candidate requiring replication/current validation.
evidenceTier.D: Practitioner, official/descriptive, market-risk, or microstructure evidence useful for architecture/context rather than direct research confidence.
evidenceTier.SYNTHESIS: Resolution or explicit synthesis item summarizing other evidence; never counted as an independent study.
evidenceTier.INFERENCE: Architecture/market-structure inference rather than a direct empirical research result; usable as caution/design context only.

retrievalHierarchy: Exact sport + exact market class + exact timing/mechanism
Indirect analogy only when explicitly labeled
No reliable direct prior -> NR rather than forced analogy

favorite_longshot_sport_specificity.title: Favorite/longshot effects are sport-, book-, and market-dependent
favorite_longshot_sport_specificity.canonicalInterpretation: Do not apply a universal favorite/longshot correction. Use the direct sport/market evidence first; older MLB/NHL reverse-FLB findings remain historical priors requiring modern validation.

devig_margin_methods.title: De-vig and margin allocation
devig_margin_methods.canonicalInterpretation: Use proportional no-vig as baseline. Where market structure warrants, compare Shin/power/book-aware alternatives. Research may flag method risk but does not silently change the current fair-value model at R3.

movement_information_vs_overreaction.title: Line movement can contain information and also overreact
movement_information_vs_overreaction.canonicalInterpretation: Movement is informative but non-monotonic. Interpret path, reversal, timing and current price rather than treating all steam as truth or all reversals as fades.

nba_totals_era_drift.title: NBA totals findings changed across eras
nba_totals_era_drift.canonicalInterpretation: Older high-total and early-season findings are hypothesis/context only. Modern-era replication weakens transport of fixed historical thresholds; current-era calibration is required.

nfl_efficiency_and_edge_decay.title: NFL efficiency, anomaly fragility, and edge decay
nfl_efficiency_and_edge_decay.canonicalInterpretation: The default NFL prior is high market efficiency and anomaly decay. Older or sample-specific patterns may generate questions but require current price, replication and holdout support.

nhl_reverse_flb_transportability.title: Historical NHL reverse-FLB versus modern transportability
nhl_reverse_flb_transportability.canonicalInterpretation: The old NHL anomaly appears historically real, but its modern multi-book transportability is not established. History Fit should preserve both facts.

nhl_totals_efficiency.title: NHL totals efficiency
nhl_totals_efficiency.canonicalInterpretation: NHL totals show some forecastability in historical work but limited easy profitability; treat the market as generally efficient and avoid heuristic systems.

boxing_research_boundary.title: Boxing has some odds-based research but remains locally calibrated
boxing_research_boundary.canonicalInterpretation: Later research resolves the strongest version of the gap: serious odds-based academic work exists, but broad boxing efficiency/calibration evidence remains too thin to replace local fight-winner calibration.

boxing_derivatives_separation.title: Boxing derivative markets stay separate from fight winner
boxing_derivatives_separation.canonicalInterpretation: Method, round and total-round derivatives must not inherit fight-winner calibration. Direct local evidence is required.

cfl_pregame_live_split.title: CFL pregame evidence gap versus supported live methodology
cfl_pregame_live_split.canonicalInterpretation: CFL live modeling has supported methodology using pregame market priors, while broad CFL pregame efficiency/calibration remains a local research gap. Do not merge the two.

player_prop_evidence_boundary.title: Player-prop practitioner evidence versus peer-reviewed research gap
player_prop_evidence_boundary.canonicalInterpretation: Book-aware vig and market separation are useful design guidance, but broad production-grade peer-reviewed prop calibration remains thin. Props do not inherit game-market confidence.

prop_integrity_risk.title: Player and micro-prop integrity sensitivity
prop_integrity_risk.canonicalInterpretation: Integrity-sensitive micro/player props deserve explicit caution and stronger verification. This is a risk modifier/context, not a predictive edge.

live_information_and_execution.title: Live markets: state updates, surprise response and execution
live_information_and_execution.canonicalInterpretation: Live prices can update quickly yet still misreact to surprise; time since event, state, pregame prior and executable liquidity all matter. No static pregame calibration should be transplanted mechanically.

calibration_over_accuracy.title: Probability calibration matters more than raw pick accuracy
calibration_over_accuracy.canonicalInterpretation: Evaluate wagering models by probability calibration, Brier/log loss, CLV and EV rather than pick percentage alone.

home_advantage_context.title: Home advantage is contextual, not a universal betting boost
home_advantage_context.canonicalInterpretation: Home effects belong inside sport- and matchup-specific fair value; generic home or home-dog boosts are not justified.

soccer_market_information.title: Soccer market information, dispersion and bookmaker behavior
soccer_market_information.canonicalInterpretation: Soccer prices are highly informative but calibration varies by league, book and market structure. Best-price/consensus information and model-versus-market comparison are more useful than generic soccer trends.

v18_market_structure_transportability.title: Market structure changes what price behavior means
v18_market_structure_transportability.canonicalInterpretation: Match the historical prior to the actual price architecture and market regime. Movement, favorite/longshot behavior, and threshold demand should not be transferred mechanically across products.

v18_replication_data_quality.title: Replication and data quality outrank headline profitability
v18_replication_data_quality.canonicalInterpretation: A historical betting pattern is not transportable until data integrity and later-period behavior survive. Large samples do not rescue a correction that fails forward holdout.

v18_nfl_market_behavior.title: NFL demand behavior is not equivalent to edge
v18_nfl_market_behavior.canonicalInterpretation: Anchoring, momentum, and key-number demand can move NFL prices without providing a robust automatic betting signal. Current price and candidate-specific evidence remain primary.

v18_player_prop_directness_boundary.title: Player forecastability and sportsbook calibration are separate evidence layers
v18_player_prop_directness_boundary.canonicalInterpretation: Use mechanism evidence to judge whether a player/stat forecast is well grounded. Use direct market evidence separately to judge historical price calibration. Never promote mechanism evidence into a price edge.

v18_mlb_prop_calibration.title: MLB player props are price-first and market-specific
v18_mlb_prop_calibration.canonicalInterpretation: Strikeouts, hits, home runs and total bases do not justify a broad historical correction after forward holdout. Walks and RBIs retain only a limited, cautious calibration signal. Candidate-specific current pricing remains decisive.

v18_nhl_prop_mechanisms.title: NHL props require stat-specific mechanism evidence
v18_nhl_prop_mechanisms.canonicalInterpretation: SOG can use role/context forecastability; goalie saves should separate volume from save efficiency and avoid hot-hand assumptions. Direct closing-price calibration remains thinner than mechanism evidence.

v18_nba_wnba_prop_transportability.title: NBA player-prop evidence does not automatically transport to WNBA
v18_nba_wnba_prop_transportability.canonicalInterpretation: NBA evidence supports stat-specific basketball modeling and rejects a simple universal directional bias, but WNBA direct closing-price calibration remains an explicit gap.

v18_nfl_prop_transportability.title: NFL player-stat mechanisms are stronger than direct prop calibration
v18_nfl_prop_transportability.canonicalInterpretation: Target opportunity, catch probability, defender context and yardage distribution can improve receiving analysis, but History Fit should remain NR/caveated when asked for broad direct sportsbook-prop calibration.

v18_parlay_margin_structure.title: Multi-leg products carry structural margin caution
v18_parlay_margin_structure.canonicalInterpretation: Parlay/SGP products should receive explicit margin and dependence caution. Large historical hold does not itself define the fair price of a specific multi-leg wager.

v18_external_projection_signal_caution.title: Player-performance forecasts are inputs, not independent sportsbook edge signals
v18_external_projection_signal_caution.canonicalInterpretation: A forecast can be useful without proving sportsbook mispricing. History Fit may use independent mechanism research while reserving direct market-calibration claims for explicitly qualified price evidence.

v18_extreme_tail_market_structure.title: Extreme longshots and outlier quotes require market-structure caution
v18_extreme_tail_market_structure.canonicalInterpretation: A long price or one-book outlier is not an independent edge. Extreme tails can carry favorite-longshot bias, and quote differences can reflect liquidity/order-flow structure. Require separately supported current handicap evidence before describing the price as a serious candidate.

v18_college_football_market_structure.title: College-football direct market structure and team-total evidence
v18_college_football_market_structure.canonicalInterpretation: Use exact college-football market evidence before NFL analogy. Team-total censoring is a direct historical inefficiency candidate; demand/pricing evidence shows sportsbook behavior need not be pure forecast information. Current-era local validation remains required.

v18_wnba_game_market_era.title: WNBA game-market evidence is direct but era-sensitive
v18_wnba_game_market_era.canonicalInterpretation: Historical WNBA spread evidence may inform game-market History Fit with strong era caveats. It does not close the modern WNBA player-prop calibration gap and should not inherit NBA prop grades.

v18_mlb_rare_batter_prop_mechanisms.title: MLB rare batter props: mechanism evidence versus price calibration
v18_mlb_rare_batter_prop_mechanisms.canonicalInterpretation: Use exact prop mechanics—contact quality for doubles, attempt/success context for steals, lineup/opportunity for runs—but do not mistake mechanism evidence for direct sportsbook calibration. Rare 0.5-event props retain large uncertainty unless locally validated.

retrievalRoleRules.primary_prior: May be retrieved as direct research context. A/B/C items can contribute research evidence weight inside History Fit; they still do not count as live BET signals.
retrievalRoleRules.synthesis: Summary/resolution only. Useful for interpretation and gap statements, never an additional evidence vote.
retrievalRoleRules.inference: Design inference only. May frame caution/market separation, never treated as empirical study evidence.
